correctness.rationale: Reconstructed all quantitative claims from the Bernoulli generating polynomial: the mixed coefficient equals alpha_k, the pair-swap gap is exactly alpha_k z², and strict positivity follows from the k>=1 boundary uniqueness in Kleiner Theorem 1/Proposition 7. The constrained all-direction Hessian is isotropic with coefficient alpha_k/2; implicit differentiation of the exact binomial ratio yields unique local mean compensation alpha_k m q(1-q)/(4c). Factorial ratios prove the explicit B_k formula. Expansions using d_k~sqrt(k/8) yield B_k=4+O(k^-1/2) and sqrt(k)C_k->2sqrt2. The packaged checker was replayed and passed 438 high-precision arithmetic assertions; numeric checks are not used as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: Quantifies the intrinsic robustness cost at a recently derived sharp probability-atom crossover. Exact full-segment pair sensitivity and isotropic all-direction quadratic loss permit comparisons among heterogeneous fixed-mean Bernoulli arrays, while the explicit sharp k^-1/2 mean-compensation scale resolves how criticality shifts for small deviations. These statements are not arbitrary small-index computations or mere uniqueness restatements; the asymptotic requires a cancellation of three growing polynomial terms. Global constrained optimizers and uniform-in-k perturbations remain unproved.
